The workshop runs over **three days** at **Knight Campus Building 2**, University of Oregon — **Wednesday–Friday, June 10–12, 2026** — with an **optional Day 0** the day before (**Tuesday, June 9**). The day-by-day plan is below; every session's lecture, reading, tutorial, and Talapas script lives on the **[Materials](Materials.qmd)** page.

## What to bring

- **Your own laptop** with at least **16 GB RAM** and **~10 GB free disk** — the workshop is hands-on and there are no lab machines
- R ≥ 4.4 and RStudio Desktop installed (see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd))
- The workshop packages installed ahead of time (covered in the Tuesday **[P2 module](Materials.qmd)**; see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd))
- A power adapter — outlets are limited in the conference room

## Day 0 (optional) — Computational Refresher

Offered on **Tuesday, June 9** (same room) as **two identical 2-hour sessions** — **10:00 am – 12:00 pm** and **3:00 – 5:00 pm**. **You only need to attend one;** come to whichever fits your schedule. Bring your laptop and any install problems you couldn't solve on your own. Each session is **two prerequisite modules** — lecture, reading, and a hands-on tutorial for each are on the **[Materials](Materials.qmd)** page:

| Block | Session |
|---|---|
| Hour 1 (10:00–11:00 / 3:00–4:00) | **Module P1** — Computer System Fundamentals (computers & operating systems, HPC clusters & Talapas, logging in with VS Code, reproducible environments) |
| Hour 2 (11:00–12:00 / 4:00–5:00) | **Module P2** — R & the Command Line (shell navigation, pipes & redirection, R & RStudio, installing packages, the tidyverse) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22,78]"}

::: callout-note
**Can't make Day 0?** It's optional, but if you're new to the command line, HPC, or R, work through the two **[P1 & P2 readings](Materials.qmd)** and the **[Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd)** before Day 1.
:::

## Bonus tracks — self-paced after the workshop

Beyond the three in-person days, the workshop ships a set of **bonus modules** (raw-data Cell Ranger pipelines and downstream analyses like WGCNA, trajectory, scATAC, spatial, and FAIR) for you to work through on your own time — see **[Materials → Bonus modules](Materials.qmd)**.

## During-workshop support

The instructors will be in the room throughout the workshop. For questions outside workshop hours, email is the most reliable channel — see the [About](about.qmd) page.
